finalText:
All 4 tests pass now.

**Root cause:** `src/jobs/processOrder.js` acquired a connection with `pool.acquire()` but called `pool.release(conn)` as a plain statement after `await run(conn, order)`, not in a `finally`. Any order that failed validation (rejected) skipped the release entirely, permanently shrinking the pool by one — `pool.js` has no timeout-based reclaim, so it's a genuine leak, not a transient stall. `worker.log` confirms this: `order-4013 failed: invalid order payload` at 01:56:11, and unlike every other job, no "connection released" line follows it. Each subsequent bad order ate another connection until the pool exhausted and `acquire()` started throwing — which lines up with the 2am page.

**Fix:** routed `processOrder` through the existing `withConnection` helper (already used correctly by `handlers/api.js`), which releases in a `finally` regardless of success/failure. The stale comment explaining why it bypassed that helper no longer applied (the retry-loop reason was gone), so I removed it along with the direct acquire/release.

The test suite itself was fine — it just needed `--test "tests/*.test.js"` since `node --test tests/` doesn't glob directory files the same way on this setup.
